title: publish-release.sh must refuse unless the named run's release-gate-probe jobs all concluded success
description: For the NEXT lore/quest pair (filing only, not built; requested by opum-doc via team-lead on 2026-10-20 under DEC-182). Today scripts/publish-release.sh never reads the release-gate-probe jobs of the Release run it stages (LCLI-738 added them in release.yml, but only the publish job lists them in needs:), so on the dry-run-artifact staging path the probe gates nothing; opum-doc read run 39366418979 by hand for 0.14.1 instead. Change: publish-release.sh refuses unless every release-gate-probe job of the named run concluded success. A Windows arm may be excused only when its log shows the setup-quest Windows source-fallback refusal AND the release quest version was not installable from npm at that time. Cites DEC-204 and LCLI-738. Needs a reviewer pass (touches scripts/) and a both-ways test: all-green accepts, one red arm refuses, a Windows arm with the refusal line and an installable quest refuses.

acceptanceCriteria.text: publish-release.sh reads the named run jobs and refuses unless every release-gate-probe job concluded success
a Windows arm is excused only when its log shows the setup-quest Windows refusal and quest at the release version was not installable from npm then
tested both ways, with a mutation of the check going red

implementationNotes: DEC-204 (a4), 2026-10-20: the same Windows-probe excuse (every failed job a Windows probe arm; each arm log shows the setup-quest Windows refusal and no other ##[error] line; @opum-ai/quest@<version> not installable at the run start per npm time[version] vs created_at; every other job success) lands in scripts/promote-latest.mjs step 1 now under LCLI-744, and lands in publish-release.sh under THIS task for the next pair. The real fix, setup-quest working on Windows, belongs in the next pair plan and retires the excuse in both places.

DEC-204 (a4) ruling E, 2026-10-20: release.yml should record its dispatch inputs (publish, launcher_rc, ladybug_scale_observation) in a step summary or log, so a run publish input is readable after the fact; the REST run object carries no inputs field (measured on run 39366418979). Goes into the NEXT pair plan with the setup-quest-on-Windows fix. F (a one-run exception) was rejected; the 0.14.1 promote path uses ruling D instead: the named by-construction skips are excused only when the publish job is present and skipped.
